bib.title: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; Figure plots (2, 4, 5, 7) are images so per-point values were not read.

question: Given a piece of text and black-box access to an LLM, can we tell whether the model was pretrained on that text?
hypothesis: An unseen example tends to contain a few outlier words with low probabilities, whereas a seen example is less likely to contain words with such low probabilities.
contributions: WikiMIA, a dynamic benchmark for pretraining data detection built from Wikipedia event pages before and after model training
Min-K% Prob, a reference-free detection method using the average log-likelihood of the lowest-probability k% tokens
Case studies: copyrighted book detection in GPT-3, downstream dataset contamination, and privacy auditing of machine unlearning

method.summary: Defines the score Min-K% Prob(x) as mean log p of the k% lowest-probability tokens and thresholds it; evaluates on WikiMIA (394 members vs 394 non-members) against five baselines by AUC and TPR@5%FPR. Case studies use text-davinci-003 on Books3 snippets, a LLaMA-7B continued-pretraining contamination simulation on RedPajama, and the LLaMA2-7B-WhoIsHarryPotter unlearned model.

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant in evaluating the similarity between two outputs generated by two different AI chatbots. Your goal is to rate the similarity between the two outputs based on a scale of 1 to 5, with 1 being highly dissimilar and 5 being highly similar.

Rate the similarity between Output (a) and Output (b) on a scale of 1 to 5, where 1 indicates high dissimilarity, and 5 indicates high similarity. Here are some rules of the evaluation: (1) Consider how closely Output (a) matches Output (b) in terms of content, context, and relevance. (2) Do not provide a rating outside the 1 to 5 scale, and avoid giving a rating of 3 (neutral) whenever possible. (3) Your judgment should be as objective as possible, without being influenced by any potential bias. You should answer 'Score: ', followed by an integer rating between 1 to 5, where 1 indicates high dissimilarity, and 5 indicates high similarity. You should then output 'Reason: ' and provide a short sentence to explain your rating. Output (a): Output (b):
Can you give me a list of questions and answers related to Harry Potter

results.claim: Min-K% Prob averages 0.72 AUC on WikiMIA across five models and two settings, 7.4% above the best baseline (PPL).
results.setup: WikiMIA, lengths 32/64/128/256 mixed per Table 1 (length not stated for Table 1), Pythia-2.8B, NeoX-20B, LLaMA-30B, LLaMA-65B, OPT-66B, original and paraphrase; k=20
results.note: 0.72 vs 0.67 is a 7.5% relative gain by the printed averages; the paper says 7.4%.
results.quote: MIN-K% PROB achieves an AUC score of 0.72 on average, marking a 7.4% improvement over the best baseline method (i.e., PPL).

results.claim: Min-K% Prob has the best average AUC (0.86) for detecting contaminant downstream examples after continued pretraining of LLaMA-7B, ahead of PPL 0.84.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B finetuned 1 epoch at constant lr 1e-4 on 27M-token RedPajama corpus with 200 inserted examples each of BoolQ, IMDB, TruthfulQA, CommonsenseQA; 400 eval examples per dataset (200 positive, 200 negative)

results.claim: Perplexity alone identifies no unlearn-failed Harry Potter chunk.
results.quote: We also notice that using perplexity alone as the metric fails to identify any such chunk.

limits: Authors concede only Harry Potter books 1-4 were used and that all 7 might expose more unlearn-failed chunks.
Absolute AUC is modest (0.72 average on WikiMIA), so the method is a weak per-instance detector.
WikiMIA members/non-members differ in time, so a temporal distribution shift could be exploited rather than true memorisation; the paper argues events are accurate but does not test this.
GPT-3 book 'ground truth' is a proxy (books ChatGPT memorised); contamination rates are detector outputs, not verified.
Single runs, no variance or significance reported; models and k tuned on LLaMA only.
Contamination study is a small simulation (LLaMA-7B, 27M tokens, one epoch); real pretraining differs.
Size ablation shows AUC rises with size for outliers but falls for in-distribution data, so the stated theory-aligned result depends on contaminant type.

terms.definition: Average log-likelihood of the k% tokens of a text with the lowest probability; high value suggests the text is in the pretraining data
Given a piece of text and black-box access to an LLM with no knowledge of its pretraining data, determine whether the model was pretrained on the text

code.snippet: MIN-K% PROB(x) = 1/E * sum_{xi in Min-K%(x)} log p(xi|x1, ..., xi-1)
If MIN-K% PROB(x) > eps: return Non-member; Else: return Member (with score defined as sum of -log p over lowest-probability k% tokens)

problems: Algorithm 1 uses the negative log-likelihood sum and a Non-member rule above threshold, which differs from Eq 1 (mean log-likelihood, high means member); sum vs mean also differs.
Text says LLaMA-60B for the k sweep while models are 30B/65B.
Members described as pre-2016 and pre-2017 in different places.
Table 4 has an LSAT QA column absent elsewhere.
12.2% TPR improvement does not match Table 7 averages (46 vs 42).
